Summary: This bill would prohibit the advertisement of any motorized scooter, limited use motorcycle, or motorcycle as a powered bicycle or a powered mobility device. An advertisement for a limited use motorcycle or a motorcycle would have to include a statement that such limited use motorcycle or motorcycle is required to be registered with the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles. The Department of Consumer and Worker Protection would have to develop materials and conduct outreach regarding powered bicycles and powered mobility devices that may be operated in accordance with applicable law.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to prohibiting the advertisement of limited use motorcycles, motorcycles, and motorized scooters as powered bicycles or powered mobility devices and related outreach

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Section 20-609 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding new definitions of “limited use motorcycle,” “motorcycle,” and “motorized scooter” in alphabetical order to read as follows: 
Limited use motorcycle. The term “limited use motorcycle” has the same meaning as set forth in section 121-b of the vehicle and traffic law.
Motorcycle. The term “motorcycle” has the same meaning as set forth in section 123 of the vehicle and traffic law. 
Motorized scooter. The term “motorized scooter” has the same meaning as set forth in section 19-176.2. 
§ 2. Subdivision f of section 20-610 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as amended by local law number 50 for the year 2024, and subdivisions h and i of such section, as added by such local law, are amended, and new subdivisions k and l are added to such section, to read as follows:
f. A person who violates this section, or any rule promulgated thereunder, is liable for a civil penalty as follows:
1. For [the] a first violation, a civil penalty of [zero dollars] $0, except that a person is liable for a civil penalty of $1,000 for a first violation of subdivision k or l of this section; [and]
2. For each subsequent violation of subdivision a, b [or], c, k, or l of this section issued on a different day within [two] 2 years of the date of a first violation, a civil penalty of not more than [two thousand dollars] $2,000; and
3. For each subsequent violation of subdivision e or h of this section issued on a different day within [two] 2 years of the date of a first violation, a civil penalty of not more than [five hundred dollars] $500.
h. Records. Any person who distributes, sells, leases, rents, or offers to sell, lease, or rent a powered bicycle, powered mobility device, or storage battery for a powered bicycle or powered mobility device shall maintain proof of certification that each such bicycle, device, or battery complies with under this section. All records required by this subdivision or by the commissioner by rule shall be maintained for [three] 3 years and shall be made available to the [department] commissioner or the fire [department] commissioner electronically upon request, consistent with applicable law and in accordance with rules promulgated hereunder and with appropriate notice.
i. The commissioner, or the fire commissioner, after providing notice and an opportunity to be heard, shall be authorized to order the sealing of any premises where any person has been found:
1. [to] To have violated this section on at least [three] 3 occasions within a [three-year] 3-year period; or
2. [to] To have violated any rule promulgated pursuant to this section, on at least [three] 3 occasions within a [three-year] 3-year period.
k. No person shall advertise for sale, lease, rent, or distribution as a powered bicycle or a powered mobility device: (i) a motorized scooter; (ii) a limited use motorcycle; or (iii) a motorcycle.
l. Any advertisement for the sale, lease, rent, or distribution of a limited use motorcycle or a motorcycle shall include a statement that such limited use motorcycle or motorcycle is required to be registered with the department of motor vehicles.
§ 3. Subdivisions b, c, and d of section 20-610.1 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by local law number 49 for the year 2024, are amended to read as follows:
b. 1. The commissioner shall, in coordination with the fire [department] commissioner, develop informational materials regarding lithium-ion and other storage battery safety, to be posted by powered bicycle or powered mobility device businesses.
2. The commissioner shall, in coordination with the commissioner of transportation, develop informational materials regarding powered bicycles and powered mobility devices that a person may operate on a street in accordance with applicable law, to be posted by powered bicycle or powered mobility device businesses. 
3. The materials required to be developed pursuant to this subdivision shall be made available in the designated citywide languages.
c. Powered bicycle or powered mobility device businesses shall conspicuously post [such] the materials required to be developed pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2 of subdivision b of this section near the location where powered bicycles or powered mobility devices are offered for sale, lease, or rent, and shall offer copies of such materials to any person at the point of sale.
d. Powered bicycle or powered mobility device businesses operating an online retail platform shall conspicuously post a hyperlink to [such] the materials required to be developed pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2 of subdivision b of this section from each webpage where powered bicycles or powered mobility devices are offered for sale, lease, or rent.
§ 4. This local law takes effect 180 days after it becomes law.
